name: African American and African Studies
department: Carter G. Woodson Institute for African-American and African Studies

declaration.notes: Older Record (catoid=61) says students must have taken or be enrolled in AAS 1010/1020 to declare; course list not legible on the page fetched.

requirements.label: Race and politics
requirements.note: One 3-credit AAS course on race and politics or an approved course in another department.

requirements.label: Humanities
requirements.note: AAS humanities course or an APPROVED course from the listed departments; not every course in those subjects counts. Language courses do not count.

requirements.label: Social sciences or history
requirements.note: AAS social science/history course or an APPROVED course from American Studies, Anthropology, Economics, Linguistics, Politics, Psychology, Sociology, WGS. Approval required for non-AAS courses.

requirements.label: Electives
requirements.note: AAS or approved courses in other departments. At most one AAS 4993 independent study may count, only as an elective.

requirements.label: 4000-level seminar with 20-page research paper
requirements.note: A non-AAS 4000-level seminar may count if the paper is submitted to the DUP.

requirements.label: Upper-level: three courses at 3000+ (besides the seminar)
requirements.note: Overlaps with the categories above; approved non-AAS 3000+ courses also count.

requirements.label: Africa focus
requirements.note: One of the seven non-core courses must focus on Africa; overlaps other categories. Cannot be determined from course number alone.

notes: 9 courses, at least 29 credits. AAS 1010 and 1020 need C or better; major GPA at least 2.0. Max 6 study-abroad transfer credits (DUP permission). Normally max 2 courses double-counted with another major (3 if other major is interdisciplinary). AAS 4993 requires 3.0 cumulative GPA. Categories overlap (Africa course and 3000+ courses count toward other categories). Requirements from department site; 2026-27 Record page (catoid=72) could not be loaded.

name: American Studies

declaration.notes: Prerequisite: at least one university-level course (UVA or college transfer, not AP/IB) in American history or culture, broadly defined, with grade C or better. Declaring in 2nd or 3rd year encouraged.

requirements.label: Theories and Methods of American Studies
Advanced seminar (4000/5000 level)
requirements.note: From the department's list of approved 4000/5000-level AMST courses.

requirements.label: Electives (7 courses, 21 credits)
requirements.note: Any AMST, AAS, HIUS or HILA course counts; other courses by petition. At least 2 must be AMST and at least 3 at 3000+. Must include one each from Historical Approaches, Race/Ethnicity, Transnational/Regional categories (one course per category).

notes: 30 credits, all C or better. Across the major 5 courses must be AMST and 5 at 3000+. Elective categories (Historical Approaches, Race/Ethnicity, Transnational/Regional) are assigned per course in SIS; not modelled by course number. Requirements from department site; 2026-27 Record page not loaded.

name: Anthropology

declaration.notes: Normally at least 18 credits must be taken after declaring.

requirements.label: Foundation
requirements.note: Faculty recommend both; DMP students normally take both.

requirements.label: Distribution: sociocultural anthropology
requirements.note: Must be a course designated sociocultural; area designation not derivable from number.

requirements.label: Distribution: archaeology
requirements.note: Must be a course designated archaeology (e.g. ANTH 2800 Introduction to Archaeology).

requirements.label: Distribution: linguistic anthropology
requirements.note: Must be a course designated linguistic (e.g. ANTH 2400, ANTH 2415).

requirements.label: Upper-level electives (3000+, taken at UVA, besides foundation and capstone)
requirements.note: May overlap with the distribution areas.

requirements.label: Total: 11 courses in ANTH (up to 2 approved outside courses)

notes: 11 courses / 33 credits. C- or better in every major course; no CR/NC. Up to 2 approved outside courses (transfer, study abroad, related disciplines) may count, normally not toward the 3000-level requirement. Area designation (sociocultural/archaeology/linguistic) of each course not modelled. Concentrations exist (see department). Source: department site; 2026-27 Record page could not be loaded (records.ureg pages returned empty / rate limited).

name: Anthropology

requirements.label: Distribution: sociocultural anthropology
requirements.note: Course designated sociocultural.

requirements.label: Distribution: archaeology
requirements.note: Course designated archaeology.

requirements.label: Distribution: linguistic anthropology
requirements.note: Course designated linguistic.

notes: 6 three-credit courses (18 credits). No level requirement. Courses from other disciplines do not count; one ANTH course from another institution may count with DUP approval. Area designation not modelled. Department site; Record not verified.

name: Archaeology

requirements.label: Core courses
requirements.note: Introduction to Archaeology, Introduction to Classical Archaeology, archaeological field methods.

requirements.label: Area/issue courses in archaeology
requirements.note: Courses on specific areas and issues of archaeological research; must be archaeology courses approved by the Program Director/advisor.

requirements.label: Related-area courses
requirements.note: Chosen with the Program Director or advisor (e.g. Classics, Religious Studies, Chemistry, Biology, Environmental Sciences).
